subject: Trial onramp — scheduling evaluation deep dive and plan
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medsol.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Trial onramp — initial plan & proposed windows

Hi Elena — thanks again for a productive discovery call this morning. Quick recap and a proposed path to get an evaluation running: 

Summary of discovery (high-level)
- Primary use case: contextual summarization + assisted triage for clinician notes (batch and near-real-time).
- Key constraints: US data residency, PII controls, latency target ~200ms for 512-token inference in production.
- Success criteria: accuracy on our prompt set (NDCG/ROUGE check), latency under target, and integrated audit/logs for compliance.

Proposed next step: 60–75 minute evaluation deep-dive (technical demo + trial plan + success criteria alignment). Please pick a slot that works for your team (we'll invite the security and platform folks you mentioned):
- Tue Oct 12, 10:00–11:15 AM PT
- Wed Oct 13, 1:00–2:15 PM PT
- Thu Oct 14, 9:30–10:45 AM PT

Agenda (draft)
1) 15m — short recap of requirements + success criteria (you lead)
2) 25m — technical deep dive (Ben) — model variants, latency/cost tradeoffs, data handling
3) 20m — trial plan & measurement approach (Neha) — prompt set, eval harness, ramps
4) 10m — security/compliance Q&A (open to your security contact)

Prep items we need from you before the call:
- Representative prompt set / 20–30 sample items (or dataset link)
- Any specific latency/throughput targets by endpoint
- Contact for security/compliance (email for invite)

I attached the call notes from today and a short pre-demo questionnaire we can use to tailor the session. If none of the windows work, propose two alternatives and we’ll adjust.

Best,

Lauren Bishop
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachment: 20261005-discovery-notes.pdf (summary, redacted PII)
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medsol.com>

Cc: Aaron Patel <aaron.patel@medsol.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Trial onramp — initial plan & proposed windows

Hi Lauren — thanks for the summary and the clear agenda. Wed Oct 13, 1:00–2:15 PM PT works best for us. Please include our security lead (security@medsol.com) on the invite — they'll want to review data handling and audit logs.

Quick note on success criteria from our side:
- Latency: median < 200ms at 512 tokens; 95th < 350ms during peak testing.
- Quality: maintain current clinician note extraction F1 within 2 pts of our baseline on the sample set.
- Controls: request for audit logs (per-request metadata) and the ability to disable model outputs containing PHI.

I'll send a short packet (security-reqs.docx) to your inbox for the team to review before the call.

Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of Data Products, MedSol Health

Thanks Elena — confirmed for Wed 10/13, 1:00–2:15 PM PT. I'll prepare:
- A short latency/cost tradeoff deck (quantized vs fp16)
- A sandbox plan for the trial (sample endpoints, token budgets, KV cache recommendations)
- A short pre-demo questionnaire (fillable) for Elena's team to populate — attaching here for Lauren to include in the invite.

Two quick ops questions for Lauren/Neha before I finalize the deck:
1) Do we want to propose a short smoke test (10k tokens, synthetic load) the first week of the trial to validate performance?
2) Are we committing to US-only residency for the evaluation environment, or is a hosted but US-region-specified environment sufficient?

Ben
